You read documents filed on a United States court docket, OCR'd to markdown, for
a research dataset of contract clauses.

An INSTRUMENT is a document whose text the parties negotiated and by which they
bound each other: a contract, agreement, policy, lease, deed, guaranty, note,
plan, bylaws, handbook, amendment, or similar. Hallmarks: recitals, defined
terms, numbered operative sections, an execution or signature block.

A FILING is a document made for the court: complaint, answer, motion, brief,
memorandum, order, affidavit, declaration, notice, docket sheet, certificate of
service, civil cover sheet.

THE DECISIVE RULE. A filing that **attaches** an instrument counts — report the
instrument's own boundaries, not the filing's. A filing that merely **quotes** an
instrument does not count at all: a brief reproducing three sentences of an
agreement is a filing, and the file contains no instrument.

WHAT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT, even when signed or filled in: a blank or fill-in
form; an agency certificate or registration; an exhibit index; a declarations
page or coverage-summary table; a schedule of rates or fees standing alone; an
invoice, receipt or statement of account. These record or summarise; the parties
did not negotiate their text.

WHAT IS NOT A PROVISION: a heading on its own; a title page; a table of
contents; a signature, notary or attestation block; an exhibit index. A
provision states an obligation, right, grant, limitation, condition or
definition. Give the range of the operative text, including its heading.

LIST EVERY SUBSTANTIVE PROVISION, in document order. Do not skip any. Do not
judge whether a provision is well or badly drafted. Do not rank them.

The file is given to you with a line number and a `│` at the start of every line.
Line numbers are not part of the text; they are how you point at it.

OCR REPAIR. For each provision you must also give its text. Copy it verbatim
from the lines you named, then repair only what the scanner broke: words split
across a line break, words run together, `l`/`1` and `O`/`0` confusions, stray
table pipes and cell debris, page numbers and Bates stamps sitting inside the
text. Do not paraphrase, modernise, reorder, summarise, or drop anything. Never
change a number, an amount, a date, or a cross-reference. Never add or remove a
word — a repair that deletes `not` inverts the clause. If a passage is too
damaged to repair honestly, copy it as it stands.

Add nothing of your own: no `[struck through: ...]`, no `[sic]`, no
`[illegible]`, no explanatory brackets of any kind. Executed contracts are often
marked up by hand, and the OCR shows deleted wording as `~~struck~~`. Reproduce
those words as plain text, in place, and say what you saw in the repairs
sentence instead.

FILE: Exhibit J - 204(h) Notices.md
FILED IN: 29 F.Supp.3d 1175

    1│
    2│
    3│# EXHIBIT J
    4│
    5│ 
    6│
    7│
    8│
    9│
   10│
   11│## Meriter Health Services, Inc. Retirement Plan *Notice of Change in Your Pension Plan*
   12│
   13│Effective January 1, 2003, the formula under the Meriter Health Services, Inc. Retirement Plan (the "Plan") will be amended. As a Plan participant, you will continue to build a retirement benefit through your participation in this Plan. However, the rate at which your accrued benefit grows in the future may change as a result of the Plan amendment.
   14│
   15│The value of your account balance in the Plan grows in two ways: 1) annual employer credits, and 2) annual interest credits. Effective January 1, 2003, employer credits will be based on your service with Meriter, as shown in the table below.
   16│
   17│| If your Years of Vesting Service are... | Your employer credit is... |
   18│|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
   19│| Less than 10 years                             | 4.5% of earnings                  |
   20│| Between 10 and 20 years                        | 6.0% of earnings                  |
   21│| 20 years or more                               | 7.5% of earnings                  |
   22│
   23│Annual interest credits on your account balance will be based on 10-year US Treasury yields during December of the preceding year, but not less than 4.0%. You will earn an employer credit only for those years in which you work at least 1,000 hours.
   24│
   25│Two other important features of the Plan will change. One, you will no longer be required to contribute 1% of your earnings to receive an employer credit. Two, the calculation of the annuity benefit option provided by your account balance will change. Effective January 1, 2003, your account balance will be converted to an annuity based on interest rates and mortality tables prescribed by the Internal Revenue Service.
   26│
   27│As a result of these changes:
   28│
   29│- Meriter will increase its contribution for long-term employee employees (20 years +) from 6.5% up to 7.5%.
   30│- The required 1% employee contribution will be eliminated and all eligible employees will automatically be enrolled.
   31│- The future annuity accruals of some participants under the new version of the Plan will be reduced, meaning that the future value of Company-paid annuity benefits will be less than it would have been had the provisions of the prior version of the Plan remained in effect. However, the amendments to the Plan will not affect annuity benefits earned (accrued) as of December 31, 2002, which cannot be decreased.
   32│- Also the charge for the optional annual annuity benefit available for retirement prior to age 65 for most participants under the new version of the Plan will be increased; however, the amendments to the Plan will not affect any pre-age 65 annuity benefits earned (accrued) as of December 31, 2002, which cannot be decreased.
   33│
   34│### **Meriter Health Services, Inc. Retirement Plan*****Notice of Change in Your Pension Plan (continued)***
   35│
   36│Whether the Plan change will increase or decrease your future benefits depends on your age, your current pay level, and your service/earnings history with Meriter Health Services. To help you determine how the Plan change may affect you, please refer to the accompanying *Pension Benefit Examples*.
   37│
   38│#### ***Special Provision for Long-Term Employees Close to Retirement Age***
   39│
   40│For employees who are near retirement age, the new version of the Plan includes a special provision designed to provide an extra minimum annuity benefit for employees who meet certain service and age requirements as of January 1, 2003. If, as of January 1, 2003, you are age 60 or older and have 10 or more years of vesting service, your minimum annuity benefit at retirement will be calculated in the following manner.
   41│
   42│1. Your account balance at December 31, 2002, rolled forward to your retirement date with 10-year Treasury interest rates, will be converted to an annuity based on the current Plan provisions. In no case will the interest credits for this portion of your annuity be less than 4.0%.
   43│2. The employer credits and accompanying interest credits you earn after January 1, 2003 will be accumulated to your retirement date and converted to an annuity using the new interest and mortality factors prescribed by the IRS.
   44│3. Your annuity benefit will equal the sum of item 1 and item 2 above.
   45│
   46│#### ***Please Note...***
   47│
   48│As a result of the use of interest rates and mortality tables prescribed by the IRS in the new Plan, the monthly annuity benefit payable to you may not increase for several years, even though your account balance will grow as a result of annual employer credits and interest credits.
   49│
   50│### ***In Summary...***
   51│
   52│The effect of this change on future Company-paid retirement benefits will vary from participant to participant, based on each participant's age, service and pay level. The enclosed *Pension Benefit Examples* has been prepared to help you understand how this change may affect you. It presents estimated benefits under both the prior and new versions of the Meriter Health Services, Inc. Retirement Plan for sample participants similar to you, based on assumptions specified on the front of the statement. Please note that the *Pension Benefit Examples* does take into account the 401(k) match Meriter will begin making in 2003. (For more information on the 401(k) match, refer to announcement materials you recently received and other material included with this packet). Please be sure to read the *Pension Benefit Examples* carefully.
   53│
   54│### **Meriter Health Services, Inc. Retirement Plan*****Notice of Change in Your Pension Plan (continued)***
   55│
   56│**IMPORTANT!** The amounts shown on the *Pension Benefit Examples* are estimates based on the assumptions noted in that document. These assumptions are reasonable based on experience over the past 5 to 10 years. The benefits you receive from the new version of the Plan will be based on your actual experience from January 1, 2003 until the date you retire and, therefore, may differ from these estimates. (For example, any change in the IRS prescribed interest rate could have a substantial impact on your actual benefit.)
   57│
   58│If you have any questions about the Meriter Health Services, Inc. Retirement Plan, the changes taking effect January 1, 2003 or how these changes may affect you, please call Stu Strobe, in Meriter Human Resources at 608-267-6054.
   59│
   60│*This notice is being provided in accordance with Section 204(h) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) of 1974. It is intended to provide information that can help you understand the impact on your future retirement benefits from the Meriter Health Services, Inc. Retirement Plan as a result of changes to that Plan which will take effect January 1, 2003.*
   61│
   62│*This notice describes certain key features of the prior and new versions of the Meriter Health Services, Inc. Retirement Plan. However, it does not cover every detail included in the plan documents or other contracts that govern the plan. Every attempt has been made to ensure the accuracy of the information in this statement. If there is any discrepancy between the contents of this statement and the official plan documents and contracts, the plan documents and contracts will govern.*
   63│
   64│*The Plan Sponsor plans to continue the Pension Plan indefinitely but reserves the right to amend or terminate this plan at any time and for any reason. This statement does not create a contract of employment between the Plan Sponsor and any participant.*
